source: audio-tools model-policy review (MATURATION-PROGRAM.md Phase 4) plus vendor model cards; uncertain values are stated as uncertain in notes; GPT-Live published model card and pricing (accessed 2026-11-20)
notes: Model choice is data plus evidence. This seed declares static facts; the selector applies policy; the qualification harness promotes.
readiness=available means an adapter exists and the model is expected to run. candidate, experimental, and watch are honest non-runnable or unqualified states.

Generic capability defaults require the default role. STT models may separately declare engine_defaults for an engine-scoped choice; both selection paths enforce readiness, evidence, platform, and commercial policy.

A non-available record with the default role must set allow_default=true, and availability still ranks first among default candidates, so an available promoted default is never displaced by an opt-in candidate.
provider_ids are stable health/lifecycle ids owned by internal/providercatalog. engine_ids name declared STT engines owned by internal/sttengine; non-STT records leave engine_ids empty.

Engine ids select streaming engines in StreamConfig. Unary batch routes can be explicitly selected by catalog model id through X-Audio-Model-ID. Local batch routes remain unavailable until their configured endpoint passes read-only serviceability checks.
WER is a percentage, SIM is a 0..1 similarity score, RTF is an x-realtime factor. Benchmark numbers are copied from the named source, not scenario-measured.
size_mb_approx=0 means the artifact size is not established in this seed; it is not a claim that the model is weightless.
Summarize records mirror resources/ollama/model-policy.json; drift tests cover Audio Tools' summarize.audio_tools route and the shared summarize.default/chat.small roles (including fallbacks).

artifact names the resource data artifact that supplies local weights. A conformance test proves every readiness=available local model names a declared artifact, that the artifact the whisper resource pins for WHISPER_MODEL_PATH is the registry default for whisper-local, and that each capability's default fits the declared resource budget.

A default role requires owner-referenced qualified evidence for corpus quality, latency, memory, platform, and license. A code-authorized operational default may carry an explicit legacy_exception that names its evidence gap; it remains unqualified.

Pricing is a published provider fact only: it does not authorize sessions, estimate spend, store credentials, or settle usage. GPT-Live active and standby rates are billed by duration; backend model/tool usage is separate.

field_reference.name: human display name
field_reference.provider_ids: stable provider ids used for health, lifecycle, and settings (must appear in known_provider_ids)
field_reference.engine_ids: STT engine ids (sttengine manifest ids); empty for non-STT records and remote BYOK/gateway/browser providers
field_reference.engine_defaults: engine ids for which this model is the explicit model default; each id must also occur in engine_ids, and a single model may be declared per capability/engine
field_reference.runtime: execution backend (whisper.cpp | kyutai | sherpa-onnx | kokoro | onnxruntime | pytorch | vllm | byok | gateway | browser)
field_reference.runtime_model_id: model identifier passed to a resource protocol when it differs from the canonical registry id
field_reference.batch_adapter_id: declared protocol adapter used for explicit local batch routes; models can share an implemented adapter
field_reference.artifact: resource artifact identity for local weights: {resource, name}; resource.json owns URL, checksum, size, and install layout. Required for readiness=available local runtimes.
field_reference.size_mb_approx: approximate primary artifact download size in MB; 0 = not established
field_reference.params: parameter count as published, or unknown
field_reference.commercial_use: yes | no | unknown; no and unknown require license_notes
field_reference.allow_default: explicit opt-in allowing a non-available record to carry a generic default role or an engine-scoped default
field_reference.hardware: cpu_capable, gpu_required, min_vram_gb, min_ram_gb, os_arch (empty = no constraint)
field_reference.benchmarks: wer, sim, rtf, or notes; nil means not established
field_reference.promotion_evidence: owner-referenced qualified receipts for corpus_quality, latency, memory, platform, and license; legacy_exception preserves an existing unqualified default without claiming a pass
field_reference.pricing: currency, unit, integer active_micros_per_minute and standby_micros_per_minute, billing_increment_seconds, and source_url; published provider facts only, never settlement policy

models.name: Whisper Medium (multilingual)
models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19, same host and harness as the turbo receipt: canonical clip WER 0.00; 61-minute fixture 52.8 s wall (RTF 69.3x); Vulkan GPU residency 1,861 MiB. Retained as the rollback/comparison baseline, not as a broad quality claim.

models.notes: ggml-medium.bin is about 1.5 GB and is acquired on demand (group "medium-model") rather than installed with every resource. Batch-only in audio-tools; whisper.cpp declares no native streaming. It carries the quality role as the rollback/comparison model, not the default.

models.name: Whisper Large v3 Turbo (multilingual)

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical clip WER 0.00; 61-minute fixture 30.3 s wall (RTF 120x); Vulkan residency 1,817 MiB. Quality tier; not a device matrix.

models.notes: ggml-large-v3-turbo.bin is the accuracy tier, not the shipped default. It is an on-demand artifact (group "turbo-model") because the resource-conscious default is whisper-small. Choose it when dictation accuracy matters more than ~1.3 GB of GPU/VRAM.

models.license_notes: OpenAI Whisper weights and the whisper.cpp runtime are MIT-licensed.

benchmarks.notes: audio-tools receipt 2026-11-19 (one Linux/Vulkan host, RTX 4070 Ti SUPER): canonical 'the quick brown fox jumps' clip transcribed exactly (WER 0.00); warm wall 0.31 s for 1.95 s audio (RTF 6.3x). 2026-11-20 product-path check returned the same transcript in 75 ms with whisper-small identified as the served model; measured VRAM residency was 716 MiB. One clean clip on one host, not a dictation-quality, timestamp-drift, or device-matrix claim.

models.notes: ggml-small.bin is the shipped runtime default (eager artifact): 488 MB on disk, about one third of turbo. It preserves multilingual support and passes the canonical quality clip exactly, while cutting the resident footprint enough to leave the GPU free for other work.

models.name: sherpa-onnx Zipformer English (2023-06-26, streaming)
models.license_notes: The upstream model card declares Apache-2.0 for the Zipformer model weights. The model is trained on LibriSpeech; dataset provenance does not change the declared model-weight license. Legal review may separately assess any obligations tied to training-data use.

promotion_evidence.legacy_exception: Existing operator-selected Sherpa streaming route retained pending joined corpus-quality, latency, memory, platform, and license receipts.

benchmarks.notes: 2026-11-20 one-host check: 310 MB archive. Transcribed the canonical Kokoro clip as "The quick brown fox jumps over the laz." and the JFK sample with substitutions. Upstream CLI shows the same model-level errors; the server path is complete. 2026-11-22 native server and WebSocket smoke on the 1.955-second five-word quality fixture returned "The quick brown, fox jumps." (lexical WER 0.00), with 147 ms warm inference (RTF 13.29x) and 3.04 s model load. This narrow clean-speech result does not remove the JFK counterexamples or qualify general dictation quality.

models.notes: The sherpa streaming runtime default: 310 MB extracted. It is roughly 7x smaller than Kyutai 1B and works end to end. Upstream quality on the JFK sample is imperfect ("And so" -> "and saw"), so this is a low-footprint tier, not a dictation-quality claim. The upstream model card declares Apache-2.0 for the weights; see license notes for training-data provenance.

models.name: sherpa-onnx Zipformer English 20M (2023-02-17, streaming)
models.license_notes: The pinned upstream ONNX model card declares Apache-2.0. Upstream says the model is trained on LibriSpeech; its dataset provenance does not change the model-card license declaration.

benchmarks.notes: No audio-tools corpus quality, latency, memory, or platform receipt exists. Upstream documentation lists the English 20M model and demonstrates real-time sherpa-onnx decoding; its int8 encoder and joiner plus fp32 decoder total about 44 MB, while the full Hugging Face repository contains about 136 MB including fp32 alternatives.

models.notes: Registry-only candidate. The existing sherpa-onnx online Zipformer runtime is protocol-compatible with this model's encoder/decoder/joiner layout, but the managed resource pins and loads the 310 MB 2023-06-26 model and has no selectable model-dir route. No artifact is declared or acquired for this candidate, and no model default changes. Add a separately pinned resource artifact and runtime selection only after checksum, corpus quality, latency, memory, and platform qualification.

models.name: Sherpa Kroko English Zipformer (streaming)
models.license_notes: The Kroko community model is CC-BY-SA-4.0: commercial use is permitted but derivative distributions carry share-alike and attribution obligations. Kroko sells a separate commercial/OEM licence. Treat a commercial deployment as requiring a licence review until the operator confirms one.

benchmarks.notes: 2026-11-20 one-host check: upstream file CLI transcribed the full clip; the WebSocket server path stopped after ~1.4 s on the 2.6 s clip. Treat as an adapter bug, not a model-quality verdict. 2026-11-24 follow-up: the native model and WebSocket smoke tests pass on an 11 s JFK fixture; at 100 ms packet cadence first text arrived after 1.5 s of captured audio, and the checked reference opening/final suffix matched. One clean utterance only: no percentile, held-out corpus, memory, platform, timestamp, or commercial-license qualification.

models.notes: On-demand 68 MB Kroko community model. A bounded 1.2 s finalization tail fixes the reproduced JFK ending truncation in the native streaming adapter. Keep it experimental pending corpus quality, latency, timestamp, and license qualification; this smoke result does not justify changing the runtime default.

models.name: Rumble 2 Flash (batch ASR, 45 languages)
models.license_notes: Apache-2.0 per the upstream model card.

benchmarks.notes: Open ASR Leaderboard English average WER 6.60; RTFx 6338. Batch benchmark only, not an audio-tools latency receipt.

models.notes: Batch ASR, not native streaming. The public model repository is 1.39 GB (1.02 GB main safetensors plus a 357 MB CTC head). Exact runtime RAM/VRAM requirements are unmeasured; the 2 GB VRAM value is only a registry lower-bound estimate, not a qualification. The upstream model card documents vLLM and Transformers GPU-oriented paths. This is not a default: the opt-in endpoint adapter exists; explicit unary selection remains unavailable unless the configured endpoint serves this model. No managed resource exists and quality/runtime qualification remains open.
